originalTitle: US stocks: SpaceX quarterly revenue surges in debut results on strong growth in its Starlink business
simplifiedContent: SpaceX, a company that recently went public, has reported a big increase in revenue (92%) for the last quarter. This growth is mainly due to its Starlink business and new artificial intelligence projects. Even with this significant increase in revenue, the company still lost money because it's spending a lot on new infrastructure and future projects. This news is important because it's one of the first times SpaceX has shared its financial results publicly, and investors are closely watching to see how the company performs. The company's stock price may be affected by this news, especially with some investors soon being able to sell their shares for the first time.

originalTitle: US stocks: Dow, S&P 500 close at record highs as AI earnings impress, oil prices tumble
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the stock market: the main US stock markets, called the Dow and S&P 500, just reached their highest levels ever. This happened because many big companies, especially those working with artificial intelligence, reported very good earnings. At the same time, oil prices went down, which helps the economy, and there's hope that a conflict in Iran might be resolved peacefully, making investors feel more confident. As a result, investors are feeling optimistic because companies are doing better than expected, which is good news for the stock market. This is a positive sign for the overall economy and the stock market.

originalTitle: US Treasury yields fall as oil retreats on Iran deal hopes, Fed hike bets ease
simplifiedContent: Here's a simplified version of the news: US Treasury yields, which is a measure of how much the government pays to borrow money, went down on Tuesday. This happened because oil prices dropped due to hopes of a deal with Iran, which makes people less worried about inflation (prices rising too fast). As a result, investors think the Federal Reserve might not raise interest rates as much as they thought, which also contributed to the drop in Treasury yields. This matters because it can affect how much it costs to borrow money and can impact the overall economy. The government will soon announce how much it plans to borrow, which is also relevant to this situation.

originalTitle: Yen holds most gains as intervention keeps speculators on edge
simplifiedContent: The value of the Japanese yen has gone up and is staying high. This is because the government has been taking steps to control its value, which is making investors nervous. As a result, people who try to make money by guessing which way the yen's value will go are being cautious and not making many moves. This means that the yen's high value is likely to stay for now. The government's actions are important because they can affect the overall foreign exchange market.

originalTitle: Palantir Short Sellers Take $3 Billion Hit After 30% Stock Surge
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: Palantir Technologies Inc.'s stock price recently went up by 30%. This is bad news for some investors, known as short sellers, who had bet that the stock price would go down. Because the stock price actually went up, these short sellers have lost a lot of money - about $3 billion. This means that all the gains they had made so far this year have been wiped out, and now they're facing big losses. This matters because it shows how quickly things can change in the stock market and how risky it can be to bet against a company's success.

originalTitle: CBOT grains, soybeans fall as oil drops on Iran hopes
simplifiedContent: The prices of grains and soybeans on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) have gone down. This happened because the price of oil also decreased, and that's related to hopes of a resolution with Iran. When oil prices drop, it can affect the prices of other commodities like grains and soybeans. This matters to investors because it can impact the value of their investments in these areas. The drop in prices is a result of changing global events and market expectations, specifically related to Iran.
